title: Corn and Avocado Salad

items.raw: 2 tablespoons olive oil, for the grill
2 ripe but firm avocados, cut into ½-inch dice
½ small red onion, finely diced
½ cup crumbled feta or cotija (optional)

steps.text: Rub the ears lightly with oil and grill over medium-high heat, turning every couple of minutes, for 8 to 10 minutes — until charred in patches and just tender. A little blackening is what you want; fully blistered corn goes tough.
Let the ears cool enough to handle, then stand each one in a wide bowl and cut the kernels off. Cutting them into a bowl instead of onto a board saves you chasing corn around the kitchen.
Put the diced red onion in a small bowl of cold water for 10 minutes, then drain well. This takes the raw bite out and keeps it from dominating the salad.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper together in a large serving bowl.
Add the corn, tomatoes, drained onion, and jalapeño and toss well. Let this sit 10 minutes so the corn takes up the dressing.
Fold in the avocado and cilantro with a light hand, just two or three turns. Overmixing turns the avocado into dressing.
Scatter the cheese over the top if using, taste for salt and lime, and serve within the hour.

notes.label: Raw corn version
notes.text: in true peak season, skip the grill entirely and use the kernels raw. Sweeter, crunchier, and faster.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: everything but the avocado and cilantro can be tossed together up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerated. Fold those in at the table.

notes.label: Make it a meal
notes.text: add a can of drained black beans and serve with grilled shrimp or chicken.

notes.label: Avocado insurance
notes.text: toss the diced avocado with a squeeze of lime the moment you cut it.

openQuestion: Whose salad is this, and does it belong to a particular summer place or cookout? Also tell me whether the corn goes in raw, boiled, or grilled — I have written it grilled.
